specs.title: 灰蓝石板色涂块
specs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original production oil-paint decal atlas for a painterly 1985 coastal town building, inspired by the material color organization of Disco Elysium. Exactly four distinct isolated shapes in a 2x2 square atlas, no labels, no borders, no objects, no architecture. Each shape occupies its quadrant with a 10% clear margin. Absolutely pure black RGB 0,0,0 flat backdrop intentionally used as mask, NOT a checkerboard. Shape-first painting: broad contiguous opaque pigment masses, ragged scraped boundaries, interrupted edges, open fissures, large offset fragments, asymmetric compositional silhouettes, sparse dry scumbling. Internal neighboring hues and restrained broad value planes, not sprayed tiny dots. No glossy impasto highlights or directional shadows, no photographed paint, no regular rectangular swatches, uniform speckles, regular radial spokes or flames. Large confident quiet pigment patches with a few strong gestures, not many tiny strokes. ALL FOUR belong to ONE slate-grey color family: a middle graphite slate grey base pigment with subtle neighboring blue-grey, violet-grey and neutral grey planes. Pigment should be medium grey on black for readable masking; final darkness will be controlled by material. Top left: wide torn diagonal slab with blunt stepped edge and broad scraped interior break. Top right: offset oblong scumble with broad missing wedge and short detached chips. Bottom left: long bent knife drag, uneven wide body with two jagged interruptions. Bottom right: compact asymmetric fractured plate with three broad uneven flares. Calm muted ROOF pigment, no pale mint, ivory, bright blue, unrelated saturated accents.
